g.text: Large language models (LLMs) deployed in production systems require robust
content moderation to prevent harmful outputs.
g.title: N1 [Context] (cites=0) Large language models (LLMs) deployed in production systems require robust content moderation to prevent harmful outputs.

g.text: Safety judges—specialized models that classify responses as safe or
unsafe—have emerged as critical gatekeepers for both offline safety
benchmarking and real-time content filtering (Inan et al., 2023; Han et al.,
g.title: N2 [Prior_Work] (cites=3) Safety judges—specialized models that classify responses as safe or unsafe—have emerged as critical gatekeepers for both offline safety benchmarking and real-time content filtering (Inan et al., 2023; Han et al., 2024; Zeng et al., 2024).

g.text: These judges typically process responses holistically, examining the entire
text to produce a single safety verdict.
g.title: N3 [Prior_Work] (cites=0) These judges typically process responses holistically, examining the entire text to produce a single safety verdict.

g.text: However, this holistic design creates a fundamental vulnerability.
g.title: N4 [Limitation] (cites=0) However, this holistic design creates a fundamental vulnerability.

g.text: We demonstrate that state-of-the-art safety judges can be
completely fooled by benign-padding attacks: simply prepending and
appending benign text to harmful content causes WildGuard's false
negative rate (FNR) to increase from 0.0455 to…
g.title: N5 [Result] (cites=0) We demonstrate that state-of-the-art safety judges can be completely fooled by benign-padding attacks: simply prepending and appending benign text to harmful content causes WildGuard's false negative rate (FNR) to increase from 0.0455 to 1.0, meaning every unsafe response is misclassified as safe.

g.text: This catastrophic failure occurs because benign padding dilutes the harmful
signal across a longer context, overwhelming the judge's detection
g.title: N6 [Limitation] (cites=0) This catastrophic failure occurs because benign padding dilutes the harmful signal across a longer context, overwhelming the judge's detection capability.

g.text: The natural mitigation—examining responses through smaller windows rather
g.title: N7 [Limitation] (cites=0) The natural mitigation—examining responses through smaller windows rather than holistically—introduces a new challenge.

g.text: As response length increases, more windows are scanned, and the probability
g.title: N8 [Limitation] (cites=0) As response length increases, more windows are scanned, and the probability of spurious false positives grows.

g.text: This multiple-comparisons effect is particularly problematic for
benign-padding attacks, which adversarially increase response length.
g.title: N9 [Limitation] (cites=0) This multiple-comparisons effect is particularly problematic for benign-padding attacks, which adversarially increase response length.

g.text: We propose WindowScan-Judge (WSJ), a post-hoc wrapper that combines
multi-scale windowed scanning with Length-Aware FPR Control (LA-FPR).
g.title: N10 [Method] (cites=0) We propose WindowScan-Judge (WSJ), a post-hoc wrapper that combines multi-scale windowed scanning with Length-Aware FPR Control (LA-FPR).

g.text: WSJ splits responses into overlapping windows at multiple scales, runs the
base judge on each window independently, and aggregates decisions using a
calibrated threshold that maintains false positive rate within a specified
g.title: N11 [Method: component] (cites=0) WSJ splits responses into overlapping windows at multiple scales, runs the base judge on each window independently, and aggregates decisions using a calibrated threshold that maintains false positive rate within a specified budget.

g.text: This approach achieves dramatic improvements: on prepend+append
padding, WSJ reduces WildGuard's FNR from 1.0 to 0.0091 while
g.title: N12 [Result] (cites=0) This approach achieves dramatic improvements: on prepend+append padding, WSJ reduces WildGuard's FNR from 1.0 to 0.0091 while keeping FPR controlled.

g.text: We identify and characterize the benign-padding vulnerability in
safety judges, demonstrating that holistic evaluation fails
catastrophically when harmful content is surrounded by benign
g.title: N13 [Contribution] (cites=0) We identify and characterize the benign-padding vulnerability in safety judges, demonstrating that holistic evaluation fails catastrophically when harmful content is surrounded by benign text.

g.text: We propose WindowScan-Judge, a tuning-free wrapper that enhances
any existing safety judge through multi-scale windowed scanning
g.title: N14 [Contribution] (cites=0) We propose WindowScan-Judge, a tuning-free wrapper that enhances any existing safety judge through multi-scale windowed scanning and length-aware aggregation.

g.text: We achieve 99.1% absolute FNR reduction on WildGuard while
maintaining FPR within budget, with consistent improvements across
multiple base judges including Llama Guard 3.
g.title: N15 [Contribution] (cites=0) We achieve 99.1% absolute FNR reduction on WildGuard while maintaining FPR within budget, with consistent improvements across multiple base judges including Llama Guard 3.
